OnionVPN is a privacy-first Android VPN that routes device traffic through the Tor network, with fail-closed leak protection inspired by Whonix and Mullvad. Clearnet DNS goes through DNSCrypt over Tor; .onion stays Tor-native.

• Tor tunnel — full-device VPN with kill switch (traffic blocked when Tor is down)
• DNSCrypt — app DNS over Tor SOCKS (encrypted resolvers; onion via Tor DNS)
• Interactive firewall — Via Tor / Via OVPN / Deny prompts with domain threat colours
• Domain threat lists — HaGeZi / URLhaus / ads & tracking reputation on prompts
• Per-app VPN — include or exclude apps from the tunnel (Orbot-style)
• App lock — lock the UI with your device PIN/biometric; tunnel keeps running
• Circuit tools — NEWNYM, hop view, MaxCircuitDirtiness presets (including wallets)
• Tor engines — C Tor (default) or Arti / onionmasq when available
• Bridges & Moat — censorship circumvention when Tor is blocked
• OpenVPN-over-Tor (optional) — TCP OpenVPN via Tor SOCKS so sites see a VPN IP, not a Tor exit
• Always-on / OS lockdown — harden against leaks outside the VPN
• No-logs mode — disable diagnostic buffers for everyday use

For a dedicated, cleaner setup, create an Android Private Space (Settings → Security & privacy → Private Space on Android 15+, or your OEM / GrapheneOS equivalent), install OnionVPN only there, and put the apps you want protected in that space.\n\nBenefits: separate Always-on VPN, isolated apps and data, less mixing with everyday clearnet apps, and a clearer mental model (work / private profile vs main profile). Enable Always-on VPN + lockdown for OnionVPN inside that space.
You can reopen this tip anytime from Settings → About. Revisit Settings after install to tune firewall, DNSCrypt, bridges, and per-app routing.
